info.title: Kage API
info.description: Self-hosted page fetching API. Every request but `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/openapi.json` carries an API key as `Authorization: Bearer kage_<keyid>_<secret>`. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code`; every answer carries `X-Request-Id`. A fetch that was made answers `200` whatever the site did: a block is the result's `outcome`, not an HTTP error. See docs/01-spec.md §16 and docs/runbooks/api.md.

get.summary:
Liveness probe: answers as long as the process is running. It checks no
dependency; readiness is a separate endpoint (spec §16.1).

Prometheus metrics (spec §20): Kage's own series, the personas' states
and self-test scores, and the sidecars' series merged in.

401.description: No key, or not a valid one.

get.summary:
Readiness probe: the database answers, at least one persona is ready
behind a usable proxy, and at least one sidecar answers (spec §16.1).
`503` otherwise, and from the moment the server is told to stop.

503.description: Kage cannot fetch now; `checks` says why.

get.summary:
Read the audit trail, newest first: every admin call through the API
and every change an operator made at the command line.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the page before; left out for the newest.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many events, at most 200; 50 when left out.

post.summary: Make an API key. Its token is in the answer and nowhere else.

422.description: The name, the scopes or a limit is not acceptable.

delete.summary:
Disable an API key. It stops authenticating at once; its row and its
audit trail stay. Disabling a disabled key changes nothing.

post.summary:
Give an API key a new secret. The old token stops working at once; the
new one is in the answer and nowhere else.

200.description: The key and its new token.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only personas in this state: `active`, `cooling` or `retired`.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description:
Include retired personas; without `state`, only live ones are
listed.

post.summary:
Replace a persona with a new one behind the same proxy. The new
persona inherits nothing.

409.description: `conflict`: the persona is retired, or its proxy cannot carry traffic.

post.summary:
Retire a persona: its sessions end and its http cookies are deleted at
once, its profile is archived and later deleted, and its proxy gets a
new persona at the manager's next sweep. Retiring a retired persona
changes nothing.
Run the self-tests of a persona, in the server.
post.description:
The http path is tested when the persona has one and an echo is
configured; the browser path in the persona's own context, through the
scheduler's gate and the forwarder. A failed test cools the persona
until one passes; a passed one ends a cooling that waited for it. This
may take a minute or two.

requestBody.description: Optional; `{}` tests against the operator's own echo and pages.

200.description: What the self-tests found; `passed` says whether they passed.

409.description: `conflict`: the persona is retired, held by other work, or its proxy cannot carry traffic.

post.summary:
Read the policy files again, now. An invalid file changes nothing: the
policies in force stay, and the answer says what is wrong.

422.description: `validation_failed`: a policy file is invalid; the last good policies stay in force.

get.summary: The pool and the bandwidth budget at a glance.

post.summary: Probe a proxy now: reachability, latency, the exit address, a leak.

409.description: `conflict`: the proxy is being replaced or is retired, and is not probed.

post.summary:
Ask the provider to replace a proxy, inside the replacement budget.
The proxy's persona is retired when the proxy is. A refusal by the
budget or by the provider is an `outcome`, not an error.

Delete a key's stored results before their retention ends (spec §19):
its fetches with their results and attempts, its finished jobs with
their items, and the rows of everything they kept (documents, bodies,
screenshots, PDFs), whose files go with the artifact store's next
sweep. A job that is still being worked is left alone: cancel it first.
The key itself, its sessions and its audit trail stay.

get.summary: What was kept of a page, streamed.
get.description:
The media type is the stored one. A text body that is kept compressed
is sent compressed (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) to a client that takes
it, and unpacked for one that does not.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The artifact's id, as a result names it (`art_...`).

200.description: The artifact's bytes, in its own media type.

404.description: `artifact_not_found`: no such artifact of this key, or it expired.

post.description:
The answer is `200` with the result whenever a fetch was made, whatever
the site did: a block is `outcome`, with `block` saying who and how. A
request that cannot be made as asked is a problem document with a
stable `code`. A fetch that takes longer than the server's wall time
(180 s unless configured) is answered `202` and carried on as a job
(`job_id`); `GET /v1/results/{id}` has its result when it ends, also
after a restart of the server.

202.description: The fetch outlasted the wall time and runs on.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking for it.

401.description: No key, or not a valid one.

403.description: The key lacks the `fetch` scope, or `sessions` for `session_id`.

422.description: The request cannot be made as asked; `code` says why.

429.description: A limit of the key or of the API; `Retry-After` says when.

503.description: Nothing can be fetched: no proxy pool, or the server stops.

post.description:
A `batch` (pages fetched one after another), a `flow` (a script of
steps in one browser) or a `crawl` (a site read from its seeds along
its links; it needs the `crawl` scope besides `jobs`).

`201` with the job, which then runs in the background: read it with
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}` and its items with `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/items`, or
name a `webhook` to be told. With an `Idempotency-Key` header the same
request within a day is answered `200` with the job it made the first
time (`Idempotency-Replayed: true`), and another request under that key
is `409 idempotency_key_reused`. Nothing is stored for a job that is
refused.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Names the job this request makes for a day: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters.

200.description: The job this Idempotency-Key made before.

401.description: No key, or not a valid one.

403.description: The key lacks the `jobs` scope, `crawl` for a crawl, or `sessions` for `session_id`.

422.description: The job cannot be accepted as asked; `code` says why, `item` (a batch's item, a crawl's seed) or `step` which part.

429.description: A limit of the key or of the API.

503.description: Nothing can be fetched: no proxy pool, or the server stops.

get.summary:
A job: its state, how far it has come, and how the deliveries of its
webhook stand.

404.description: `job_not_found`: no such job of this key.

post.description:
What waits is cancelled at once; an item that waits for its persona is
taken out of the queue; a page that is being fetched at this moment is
finished, so at most one more item per visitor ends after the cancel.
The answer is the job as it stands; it is `cancelled` once what was
under way is over. A job that has ended is answered as it ended.

get.summary: The items of a job, in the job's order, each with its stored result.
get.description:
A result here is what `GET /v1/results/{request_id}` returns without
the document and the body, which are artifacts (named in `artifacts`).
An item of a flow is one of its steps; the last item is the page the
flow ended on. An item of a crawl is a page the crawl asked for, in
the order it asked, with what the page was to the crawl in `crawl`;
the list grows while the crawl reads.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the page before; left out for the first page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Items per page: 50 unless said, at most 200.

parameters.name: results
parameters.description: False leaves every item's `result` out: states and outcomes only.

422.description: The cursor or the limit is not one.

get.summary: What Kage would do with a request for a host.
get.description:
The policy is resolved as a request's would be: the host's own entry,
then its parent domains', then the defaults. Nothing is fetched and no
name is looked up.

200.description: The policy in force for the host.

get.summary: The result of a fetch, by the request's id.
get.description:
`200` with the result once the fetch has ended; `202` while it runs.
What only the synchronous answer has (`pacing`, `behavior`, `console`,
`side_effects`) is null here.

202.description: The fetch is still under way.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again.

404.description: `result_not_found`: no such request of this key, or it expired.

post.summary: Open a session, or return the open one.
post.description:
`201` for a new session, `200` for one that is open under the id. The
persona is the ready one with the fewest open sessions among those the
hints and the domain's policy allow.

201.description: A new session; its persona is new to this id.

409.description: `no_matching_persona`, or `session_persona_conflict` for an open session whose persona the request excludes.

422.description: The id or a hint is not well formed.

get.summary:
Look at a session. Looking is not using: the session's idle time does
not start again.

delete.summary: End a session. Its persona goes on; the id is free again.

AssertStep.description: End the flow unless a condition holds: exactly one of the two is given.

selector.description: This CSS selector must match an element.

text_contains.description: The page's text must contain this.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

AttemptView.description: One try at a request by one persona.

persona.description: The persona that made it, as in `persona.id`.

reason.description:
Why it ended as it did when the site did not say, for example
`proxy_failed`.

seed.description: The seed its behavior and pauses were drawn from. Admin keys only.

status.description: The status of the response, when one arrived.

total_ms.description: How long it took, in milliseconds.

AuditPage.description: A page of the audit trail.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the events before these; null at the end.

AuditView.description: One entry of the audit trail.

api_key_id.description: The key, when the actor was one.

details.description: What came of it. Never a secret.

id.description: The event's id; ids sort by time.

BackStep.description: Go back one page in the tab's history.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

BatchJob.description:
A batch: pages fetched one after another the way a visitor reads them.

Per site a batch has one visitor: one persona reads its pages of that
site in the order given, in sittings, with the pauses a person makes,
and comes back after its breaks; another persona takes over only when
that one cannot go on (it was blocked there, reached its daily cap, or
is gone). A site therefore sees one household reading, not a list being
dealt out to several addresses. That costs time: under the `human`
pacing about an hour for 50 pages of one site and a day for 300, which
is the daily cap of one persona, and a batch that meets the night ends
in the morning. `visitors` trades that for speed (about 20 minutes for
50 pages with three), and a faster `pacing` does where the policy does
not lock it. Sites of one batch are independent and are read side by
side.

oneOf.description:
What every item is fetched with unless it says otherwise: any field
of a fetch request but `url` and `session_id`.

items.description:
Pages that differ from `defaults`: each a fetch request of its own,
with whatever it sets taking the place of the default. They come
after `urls`.

session_id.description:
An open session of this key: every item is fetched by the
session's persona and by no other, with a fetch's rules (the
`sessions` scope, `session_not_found`, `session_persona_conflict`).
The job counts as use of the session while it has items left.

urls.description: Pages fetched as `defaults` says, in this order.

visitors.description:
How many personas read one site for the batch at a time; 1 unless
said, at most the `domain_concurrency` of the pacing in force for
the site (3 under `human`). More is refused, not reduced.

oneOf.description: Where the job's events are posted.

webhook.secret: a secret of sixteen bytes or more

BehaviorField.description:
What the persona does on a browser page, where the request wants less
than the domain policy's default. What is left out is the policy's.
Ignored, and reported as ignored, when the policy sets
`behavior_locked`.

What it costs: with the policy's default a page takes about 35 s
(median), which is about 100 pages an hour per persona. `scroll_depth:
0.3, dwell_ms: 3000` is about 11 s a page and still looks like someone
skimming a listing; `scroll_depth: 0, dwell_ms: 3000` is about 5 s.
There is no bare load: the pointer always moves, and the dwell never
falls below the policy's `min_dwell` (2 s unless a domain says
otherwise).

dwell_ms.description:
The median of the time spent on the page after it loaded, in
milliseconds. Each attempt's dwell is drawn around it and is never
shorter than the policy's `min_dwell`. Default: the persona's own
human dwell (a median of about 6 s).

oneOf.description: How the page is arrived at. Default: the policy's.

scroll_depth.description:
How far down the page to scroll, from 0 to 1; 0 for no scrolling.
Default: drawn between 0.6 and 0.9. Scrolling with its reading
pauses is most of a page's time.

BehaviorSource.description: Whose the behavior on the page was.

BehaviorView.description: What the persona did on the page of the last browser attempt.

dwell_ms.description: The time spent on the page after it loaded, in milliseconds.

patience_ms.description:
The patience the persona had with this page, in milliseconds: how
long it would have gone on scrolling at most. Kage draws it anew
for every page; `timeout_ms` bounds reaching the page and nothing
after it. Null for a flow, which scrolls where its steps say.

referer_strategy.description: How the page was arrived at.

request_ignored.description:
Whether the request asked for behavior that the policy's lock
overrode.

scroll_depth.description:
How far the persona meant to scroll the page, from 0 to 1; 0 for
no scrolling.

oneOf.description:
Why the scrolling ended: `depth` (as far as it meant to go),
`patience` (its patience with the page ended first) or `page` (the
page does not go further); null when the page was not scrolled.

scroll_reached.description:
How far down the document it came, from 0 to 1; null when the page
was not scrolled or the browser did not say.

seed.description: The seed all of it was drawn from. Admin keys only.

confidence.description: How sure the signature is, from 0 to 1.

type.description: The kind of block, for example `managed_challenge`.

Checks.description: What readiness was found to be.

persona.description:
At least one persona is ready (active, warmed up) behind a proxy
that can carry traffic.

sidecar.description: At least one browser sidecar answers.

ClaimedOsField.description: The operating system a persona claims.

ConsoleView.description: One entry of the browser's log.

url.description: The URL it names, if any.

Counters.description: How far a job has come.

cancelled.description: Items that never ran because the job was cancelled.

pending.description: Items that are not over yet.

CrawlItemView.description: What a page of a crawl was to the crawl.

backs.description: How many pages back in its tab the persona went before the click.

content_hash.description:
The SHA-256 of what the page says, without what the site repeats on
every page, as hexadecimal.

depth.description:
The least number of links from a seed the crawl knew when it asked
for the page.

duplicate_of.description:
The page read before it that says the same word for word. Its own
links were not followed from here: they are that page's.

final_url.description: Where the page ended when a redirect led elsewhere.

found_by.description: How the crawl came to know the address: `seed`, `sitemap` or `link`.

found_on.description: The page its link was first seen on.

lastmod.description: When the site's sitemap says the page last changed.

oneOf.description: What it links to.
The page read before it that says nearly the same.
How it was reached; null when it was not.
How its scrolling ended, for a page read in a browser.

CrawlJob.description:
A crawl: a site read from its seeds along its links, the way a reader
goes through it.

One persona reads one site. Its first page is typed; every later page
is reached by a click on a link of the page that is open or of one a few
steps back in its tab, and only when the tab holds nothing more an
address is typed. It rests between pages, takes its breaks and sleeps
like every other visit, so a crawl takes the time a reader takes: under
the `human` pacing about an hour for 50 pages of one site. `visitors`
and a faster `pacing` in `defaults` trade that for speed, as in a batch.

Every page the crawl asks for is an item of the job, in the order it was
asked for, with its depth, where its link was found, how it was reached
and what it repeats.

allow.description:
Regular expressions on the normalized address (spec §13). With any,
a page is read only when one of them matches. At most 32, each at
most 512 bytes.

oneOf.description:
What every page is fetched with: any field of a fetch request but
`url`, `session_id`, `method`, `body` and `request_kind`.

deny.description:
Regular expressions on the normalized address: a page one of them
matches is never read, whatever `allow` says.

max_depth.description:
How many links from a seed a page may be, by the shortest way the
crawl finds: `crawl.default_max_depth` (3) unless said, at most 32.
0 reads the seeds only.

max_pages.description:
How many pages the crawl asks the sites for at most, a page that
failed included: `crawl.default_max_pages` (100, or `jobs.max_items`
where that is fewer) unless said, at most `jobs.max_items`.

same_site_only.description:
Whether the crawl stays on the sites of its seeds (their registrable
domains); true unless said. With false it follows a link to any
site, each with a visitor of its own, inside the same limits; every
address passes the guard against private networks before it is
asked for.

seeds.description:
Where the crawl starts: 1 to `crawl.max_seeds` (100) addresses. A
seed is read whatever `allow` says; one that `deny` matches is
refused.

session_id.description:
An open session of this key: its persona reads every page, and no
other, with a fetch's rules.

use_sitemaps.description:
Whether the sitemaps of the seeds' sites are read first and the
pages they name become places to start from; false unless said. A
reader does not ask for `/sitemap.xml`: a site that watches for the
request sees it. It is therefore made by another persona than the
one that reads the site (a scout), and never when there is none.

visitors.description:
How many personas read one site for the crawl at a time; 1 unless
said, at most the `domain_concurrency` of the pacing in force for
the site. More is refused, not reduced.

oneOf.description: Where the job's events are posted.

CrawlView.description: How far a crawl has come (spec §13).

depth_reached.description: The depth of the deepest page read.

discovered.description:
Addresses the crawl knows: its seeds, what sitemaps named and what
pages linked to, each once however often and however spelled.

dropped.description:
Addresses found after the crawl knew `crawl.max_frontier` of them:
counted and forgotten.

duplicates.description: Pages that say word for word what a page read before them says.

ended.description:
Why the crawl stopped reading: `completed` (nothing inside its
scope is left), `max_pages`, `cancelled` or `expired`; null while it
goes on.

failed.description:
Pages that could not be read: the fetch failed, or the site
answered with an error status (its item is then a fetch that
succeeded, with the status in its result).

max_depth.description: The furthest a page may be from a seed.

max_pages.description: The most pages the crawl asks for.

near_duplicates.description: Pages that say nearly what a page read before them says.

pages.description: Pages asked of the sites so far: what `max_pages` counts.

sitemaps.description: The sitemaps of a crawl with `use_sitemaps`.

skipped.description:
Addresses the crawl knows and does not read, by reason: `off_site`,
`too_deep`, `denied`, `not_allowed`, `not_a_page` (a file),
`hidden` (no reader can see the link), `already_read` (another
address redirected there), `ssrf_denied`, `robots_denied` (the
site's `robots.txt` disallows it and its policy keeps to the file).

waiting.description: Of them, pages that wait to be read.

DeliveryView.description: One event on its way to the job's webhook.

id.description: The event's id, which the receiver sees as `X-Kage-Delivery`.

last_error.description:
Why the last attempt failed when the receiver did not answer:
`timeout`, `connect`, `unresolved`, `address_denied`, …

last_status.description: The status of the last attempt, when the receiver answered.

next_attempt_at.description: When the next attempt is due, while pending.

state.description:
`pending`, `delivered`, `failed`, or `superseded` (a progress event
that a later one overtook).

ErrorCode.description:
The stable codes of the API's errors (spec §16.1). The name is
what a problem document carries as `code`.

ExtractField.description: What of a page is extracted; with `include: ["extract"]`.

links.description: Whether the links of the page are listed.

markdown.description: Whether the main content is also written as markdown.

ExtractStep.description: Capture the page as it is at this point of the flow.

oneOf.description:
What is extracted from the page as it is at this point; with
`extract`.

include.description:
What to capture: `dom`, `raw`, `headers`, `extract`, `xhr`,
`console`. `dom` and `headers` unless said.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

oneOf.description: Which responses of the page's scripts are kept; with `xhr`.

ExtractView.description:
What a page says (spec §14): read from the document the visit captured,
never by a second request.

headings.description: The headings of the main content, in order.

jsonld.description:
Every JSON-LD block that parses, a top-level array as its members;
at most 64.

jsonld_skipped.description: JSON-LD blocks left out: not JSON, too large, or beyond the 64.

lang.description: The language the document says it is in (`<html lang>`).

links.description:
The links a reader can see, in document order; null when the
request said `extract.links: false`.

links_truncated.description: Whether the page held more links than are listed.

markdown.description:
The main content as markdown: headings, lists, fenced code with its
language, tables, absolute links. Null when the request said
`extract.markdown: false`.

meta.description:
Every `<meta name>` with content, by name in lower case: its values
in document order.

modified_at.description: When the page says it was last changed, read the same way.

opengraph.description:
The OpenGraph properties (`og:`, `article:` and their kin), by
name.

published_at.description:
When the page says it was published: from its JSON-LD, else its
`article:` metadata, else other metadata, else a `<time>` of its
content. In UTC when the page named a zone, as written when not.

text.description:
The main content as text: what a reader would read, without the
navigation, the side bars and the footer.

thin_content.description:
Whether the main content has fewer words than `extract.thin_words`
(80 unless configured): the document gave a reader next to nothing.
On the http path that usually means scripts or a wall.

twitter.description: The Twitter card properties, by name.

word_count.description: How many words the main content has.

FetchAccepted.description: The answer to a fetch that is not finished: `202`.

job_id.description:
The job that carries the fetch on: `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` says where
it stands (it may be `paused`, for a site or for its persona), and
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` stops it. Null for a result that is
asked for while a job's item is still being fetched.

result.description: Where the result will be: `GET` it until it is `finished`.

oneOf.description:
What the persona does on the page, where less than the default is
wanted; not with `render: http`.

body.description:
The body of a `POST`, as text; needs `render: http` and a
`Content-Type` header.

cache_ttl_s.description:
For how many seconds the result may be served from the response
cache: a later request that asks for the same is answered with it,
without a visit, while it is no older than that request's own
`cache_ttl_s`. 0 is never. Left out, the site's policy decides
(never, unless the operator set `cache.ttl`). At most the site's
`cache.max_ttl` (a day unless configured): more is refused with
`cache_ttl_too_long`. Not in a session.

oneOf.description: What is extracted; with `include: ["extract"]`.

headers.description:
Headers of the request's own; at most 32, and only with
`render: http`. A browser sends its own headers and cannot be given
others without a page noticing. Headers that are the persona's
identity or the transport's are refused by name (`User-Agent`,
`Accept-Language`, `Accept-Encoding`, `Cookie`, `Origin`, `Sec-*`,
`Proxy-*`, `Host` and others). A `Referer` names the page the
request comes from.

include.description:
The parts of the result to return and to keep. Default: `dom` and
`headers`, or `raw` and `headers` with `render: http`.

max_body_bytes.description: The largest body and document kept, in bytes; a longer one is cut.

max_retries.description:
Retries after the first attempt, each by another persona. Default:
the policy's (2).

oneOf.description:
The pacing; ignored, and reported as ignored, when the domain's
policy locks pacing. On a browser render the gap is a floor under
the time on the page, so a faster profile shortens nothing there.
How the PDF is printed; with `include: ["pdf"]`.
Which personas the request would have.

request_kind.description:
What the request is on the http path; anything but `navigation`
needs `render: http` and a `Referer` header naming the page that
makes the request.

robots.description: What to do about the site's `robots.txt`.

oneOf.description: How the screenshot is taken; with `include: ["screenshot"]`.

session_id.description:
An open session of this key: the request is made by the session's
persona and by no other. Needs the `sessions` scope. A fetch never
opens a session; `POST /v1/sessions` does.

timeout_ms.description:
The longest one attempt may take, in milliseconds: at least 15000
when a browser may make it (`browser` and `auto`), at least 1000
with `http`, at most 300000. Default: 60000 in a browser, 30000 on
the http path.

url.description:
The page: an `http` or `https` URL of at most 8192 bytes. Hosts
that name no public site are refused (`ssrf_denied`).

oneOf.description: What a browser waits for; not with `render: http`.

Which responses of the page's scripts are kept; with
`include: ["xhr"]`.

artifacts.description:
What was stored of the page, by kind (`dom_html`, `raw_body`,
`screenshot`, `pdf`): ids for `GET /v1/artifacts/{id}`.

oneOf.description:
What the persona did on the page, for a browser attempt. For a
result served from the cache: on the visit that got the page.
Who blocked and how, when the outcome is a block.

cached.description:
Whether the result was served from the response cache: nothing was
asked of the site, `attempts` is empty, and the page is the one a
visit at `cached_at` got.

cached_at.description: When the page of a result served from the cache was fetched.

console.description:
The browser's log; with `include: ["console"]`. At most the first
1000 entries, each text cut at 4096 bytes.

dom_html.description:
The document as the browser had it after the page settled; with
`include: ["dom"]`. Null on the http path, which has no DOM: the
document is `raw_body` there.

escalated.description: Whether the request moved from the http path to a browser.

oneOf.description:
What the page says; with `include: ["extract"]`. Null for a fetch
that did not get its page and for a response that is no HTML
document.

headers.description: The headers of the main response; with `include: ["headers"]`.

id.description:
The request's id, as in `X-Request-Id`; `GET /v1/results/{id}`
returns this document again.

outcome.description:
How the request ended. A block is an outcome, not an HTTP error:
the status of this answer is 200 whenever a fetch was made.

oneOf.description:
The pacing that applied to the request. For a result served from
the cache it is the request's own, which waited for nobody.
The persona of the last attempt.

raw_body.description:
The body of the main response as text; with `include: ["raw"]`,
and on the http path with `include: ["dom"]` too. Null when the
body is not text: `artifacts.raw_body` has it then.

reason.description:
Why it ended without the site's verdict, as a stable name:
`no_persona`, `domain_paused`, `egress_unsafe`,
`bandwidth_exhausted`, `proxy_failed`, `timeout`, `interrupted`
(the server stopped while the page was being read) and others.

redirects.description: Every URL visited before `final_url`, in order.

retry_at.description:
When asking again is worth it, when Kage knows: the end of a
domain's pause or of a persona's cooldown.

oneOf.description:
What the site's `robots.txt` says of the address. Null for a
request that ended before it was looked at (a refused URL).

session_id.description: The session the request was made in.

side_effects.description:
Events a capture fired in the page (`resize` for a full-page
screenshot on chromium, `beforeprint` and `afterprint` for a PDF).

state.description:
Always `finished` here; a fetch still under way is a
[`FetchAccepted`].

status.description: The status of the last response.

timing.description: Time per phase of the last attempt.

oneOf.description: The responses the page's scripts fetched; with `include: ["xhr"]`.

FlowBehaviorField.description: What a flow may change of how its persona behaves.

dwell_ms.description:
The median of the time the persona stays on a page after arriving
there, before the next step, in milliseconds. Left out: the
persona's own. Never below the policy's `min_dwell` (2 s unless
set), and ignored where the policy locks behavior. A flow always
dwells after it arrives and always pauses between its actions:
nothing turns that off.

typos.description: Now and then type a neighbouring key, notice, delete and retype.

FlowJob.description:
A flow: a script of steps one persona performs in its browser, as one
visit.

The persona arrives by a typed navigation, stays on every page it comes
to for a while with its pointer moving, and pauses between its actions
as a person does, so a flow takes longer than its steps: plan about ten
seconds for every page it visits. A flow whose page turns out to be a
wall is a blocked attempt: the persona leaves, and another one runs the
flow again from its first step, inside the policy's retry budget (never
in a session). A step that fails on a page that is no wall is the
script's failure and is not retried. The job's items are the steps, in
order, and one last item for the page the flow ended on.

actions.description: The steps, at most 100. The first is a `goto`.

oneOf.description: What the flow may change of how its persona behaves.
What is extracted from the last page; with `include: ["extract"]`.

include.description:
What is returned and kept of the page the flow ends on: `dom` and
`headers` unless said.

max_body_bytes.description: The largest body and document kept, in bytes.

max_retries.description:
How often the flow is run again by another persona after a block.
Default: the policy's (2).

oneOf.description:
The pacing of the persona's arrival at the flow's site; ignored
where the policy locks it.
How the last page's PDF is printed; with `include: ["pdf"]`.
Which personas the flow would have.

How the last page's screenshot is taken; with `include:
["screenshot"]`.

session_id.description:
An open session of this key: its persona runs the flow, and no
other; a flow in a session is never run again after a block.

timeout_ms.description:
The whole time one run of the flow may take, in milliseconds:
180000 unless said, at least 15000, at most 300000.

oneOf.description: Where the job's events are posted.

Which responses of the last page's scripts are kept; with
`include: ["xhr"]`.
Load a page.
Click an element.
Type text into an element.
Press one key.
Scroll the page.
Wait for a condition.

allOf.description: Choose an option of a select element.

oneOf.description: Choose an option of a select element.

allOf.description: Move the pointer over an element.

oneOf.description: Move the pointer over an element.
Go back one page.
Capture the page.
Take a screenshot.
Print a PDF.

allOf.description: End the flow unless a condition holds.

oneOf.description: End the flow unless a condition holds.

FlowStepField.description:
One step of a flow, chosen by `action` (spec §10.5).

The steps that touch the page (`click`, `type`, `press`, `scroll`,
`select`, `hover`, `back`) are done with the persona's own mouse and
keyboard. The first step that fails ends the flow.

FreeForm.description: A JSON object with any members; what they are is said where it is used.

GotoStep.description: Load a page. The first step of every flow.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

url.description: The page: an `http` or `https` URL that passes the SSRF guard.

HeaderView.description: One response header. A list keeps the order and repeated names.

value.description:
The value. Of a `Set-Cookie` only the cookie's name and attributes:
its value reads `[redacted]` unless the operator exposes it.

HeadingView.description: A heading of a page's main content.

id.description: Its `id`, when it has one: the fragment that links to it.

Include.description: A part of the result a request asks for.

JobItemView.description:
One item of a job: a page of a batch or of a crawl, or a step of a
flow.

oneOf.description:
What the page was to the crawl, for an item of a crawl: its depth,
where its link was found, how it was reached, what it repeats.

error.description:
Why it failed, or was not attempted: an outcome's name, a reason
such as `domain_paused` or `cancelled`, or a step's own error.

not_before.description: Not taken up before this moment: what it waits for is not over.

oneOf.description: How its fetch or its capture ended.

request_id.description:
The id its result is stored under: `GET /v1/results/{id}` returns
it with the document and the body.

oneOf.description:
The stored result, without the document and the body (they are
artifacts, named in `artifacts`). Null while there is none, and
when the page was asked for with `results=false`.

seq.description: Its position in the job, from 0.

started_at.description: When it was first taken up.

oneOf.description: The step, for an item of a flow.

url.description: The page, for an item of a batch or of a crawl.

JobItemsPage.description: A page of a job's items.

items.description: The items, in the job's order.

next_cursor.description: What to pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last.

oneOf.description: Pages fetched one after another.

allOf.description: A script of steps in one browser.

oneOf.description: A script of steps in one browser.

allOf.description: A site read from its seeds along its links.

oneOf.description: A site read from its seeds along its links.

cancel_requested.description: Whether a cancel was asked for.

oneOf.description: How far a crawl has come; null for every other job.

deadline.description:
When it stops waiting for what holds its items: the items left then
fail with what they were waiting for.

error.description: Why the job failed as a whole, when it did.

items_url.description: Where its items are read, page by page.

origin.description:
`api` for a job that was submitted, `sync_overflow` for a fetch
that outlasted its wall time and is carried on as a job.

oneOf.description: What a paused job waits for.

session_id.description: The session the job runs in, when it names one.

type.description: What kind of job it is.

visitors.description: How many personas read one site for a batch or a crawl at a time.

oneOf.description: The job's webhook.

KeyCreated.description: A key with its token, which is shown this once.

token.description:
The token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Kage keeps only a hash
of its secret and cannot show it again.

keys.description: The keys, oldest first, disabled ones included.

KeyRequest.description: What a new key is to be.

daily_page_budget.description: Pages per day (UTC); no budget when left out.

max_concurrent.description: Requests in flight at once; 4 when left out.

name.description: A name for humans: 1 to 100 characters.

requests_per_minute.description: Requests per minute; 60 when left out.

scopes.description: What the key may do; at least one scope.

KeyView.description: An API key. Its secret is not here: only its hash is stored.

daily_page_budget.description: Pages per day (UTC); null for no budget.

id.description: The key's id; the `<keyid>` of its token, with hyphens.

last_used_at.description: When it last authenticated a request, to the minute.

rel.description: The tokens of its `rel`, in lower case.

same_site.description:
Whether it leads to a page of the site the document was loaded
from (the same registrable domain).

url.description: Where it leads, as an absolute address.

LinksView.description: The links of a page as the crawl took them.

found.description: Links a reader can follow, each address once.

new.description: Of those, the addresses the crawl did not know before this page.

LivenessStatus.description: Whether the process can answer requests.

NearDuplicateView.description: The page a page nearly repeats.

bits.description: In how many of the 64 bits of their fingerprints the two differ.

url.description: The page read before it that says nearly the same.

OutcomeField.description: How an attempt or a request ended (spec §2).

PacingField.description: The pacing a request asks for (decision D9). Give `profile` or `custom`.

oneOf.description: A profile of the request's own, in the format of that file.

profile.description: The name of a profile of `policies/pacing-profiles.yaml`.

applied.description: The profile's name; `custom` for one sent with the request.

request_ignored.description:
Whether the request asked for pacing that the policy's lock
overrode.

waited_ms.description: How long the request waited for personas and their slots.

PausedView.description: What a paused job waits for.

reason.description:
What stands in the way: `domain_paused`, `bandwidth_exhausted`,
`egress_unsafe`, `budget_exhausted`, or `no_persona` (its visitor
is on a break or asleep).

PdfField.description:
How a PDF is printed. Printing fires `beforeprint` and `afterprint` in
the page, as printing by hand does; the result names both.

PdfStep.description: Print a PDF at this point of the flow.

oneOf.description: How it is printed.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

PersonaAdminView.description: A persona, as an operator sees it.

browser_major.description: The major version of its browser.

browser_open.description: Whether its browser is open now.

country.description: The country its address is in.

oneOf.description: The stored fingerprint document; only when asked for.

http_profile.description:
The emulation profile of its http path; null for a browser-only
persona.

ready.description: Whether real work may use it: active and warmed up.

PersonaHints.description: Which personas a request would have.

countries.description:
Countries the request would rather be fetched from, as two-letter
codes. A preference, not a filter: the result says where the
persona was. Against a session's persona it is a condition.

engines.description: The engines the request accepts; empty for any the policy allows.

PersonaView.description: The persona that made a request, as its caller may know it.

country.description: The country its address is in.

id.description:
For a key without the `admin` scope a handle (`p_` and 16
hexadecimal characters) that is the same for this key and this
persona every time and means nothing to another key; for an admin
key the persona's id.

PoliciesView.description: What is in force after a reload.

domains.description: Domains with an entry of their own.

PolicyPreview.description: The policy in force for a host.

first_render.description:
The path a request with `render: auto` takes first: `http` when the
policy says so, else `browser`.

pacing_profile.description:
The pacing profile the policy names, in the format of
`policies/pacing-profiles.yaml`.

paused_until.description:
Until when the host is paused because too many requests to it were
blocked; null when it is not. A request made before then ends as
`provider_error` with reason `domain_paused`.

policy.description:
Every field of the policy as it resolves for the host: `host`,
`matched` (the entry that applies), `inherits`, `render`,
`countries`, `engines`, `pacing`, `pacing_locked`, `robots`,
`referer_strategy`, `active_hours`, `min_dwell`, `behavior_locked`,
`retries`, `breaker_threshold`, `breaker_pause`, `cooldowns`.

oneOf.description:
The bandwidth budget of the proxy plan: bytes counted by Kage and
by the provider, the cap, the share used, and whether the hard stop
is in force. Null until it was first judged.

personas.description:
The personas: how many per state and per engine, how many are
ready, and how many browsers are open.

proxies.description:
The proxies: by state, how many are usable, whether a leak is on
record, and the replacement budget of the current term.

key.description: The key as `KeyboardEvent.key` names it, for example `Enter`.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

allOf.description:
What a client needs to act on the problem: for example `header`,
`field`, `retry_after_s`, `constraint`.

code.description: The stable code clients branch on.

request_id.description: The id of the request, as in `X-Request-Id`.

title.description: What the code means; the same for every occurrence.

ProxyAdminView.description:
A proxy, as an operator sees it. Its user name and password are never
returned.

backoff_until.description: Until when it is left alone.

failing_since.description: Since when it fails without a break.

oneOf.description:
What the last probe and the last lookups found: reachability,
latency, the exit address, the observed geo record, reputation.

replacement_reason.description: Why a replacement was requested, when one was.

PurgeRequest.description: Whose stored results to delete, and up to when.

before.description:
Delete what was fetched before this moment; left out: everything
the key has fetched until now.

key_id.description: The key whose results are deleted.

artifacts.description:
Bodies, documents, screenshots and PDFs whose rows were deleted.
Their files go with the artifact store's next sweep.

jobs.description: Finished jobs, with their items and their items' results.

requests.description: Fetches that were not part of a job, with their results.

ReachedCounts.description: How the pages of a crawl were reached, in numbers.

click.description: Links clicked on the open page.

referer.description: Pages of the http path that named the page before them.

ReachedField.description: How a page of a crawl was reached.

RefererStrategyField.description: How a page is arrived at.

RenderField.description: The path a request asks for.

ReplacementView.description: What became of a request to replace a proxy.

RequestKindField.description: What a request is on the http path.

RobotsField.description:
What to do about the site's `robots.txt`. Whether the file is asked
for at all is the site's policy (`ignore` unless the operator says
otherwise): a reader never asks for it, so asking marks an address. A
request may ask for more care than the policy takes and never for
less, and never makes Kage ask a site its policy leaves alone.

RobotsView.description: What the site's `robots.txt` says of the address (spec §14).

allowed.description:
Whether the file allows the address; true when nothing is known.
Under `report` a page that is not allowed is fetched all the same.

crawl_delay.description:
The `Crawl-delay` of the group that applies, in seconds. Kept to
only where the file is enforced.

fetched.description:
Whether the verdict is the file's. False when nothing is known of
it: the site's policy never asks for it (the default), the request
said `ignore`, or the site's scout has not brought it yet.

matched_rule.description:
The line that decided, as `Allow: <pattern>` or `Disallow:
<pattern>`; null when no rule matched.

ScopeField.description: What an API key may do.

format.description:
The image format; WebP unless said. A firefox persona's browser
encodes PNG and JPEG only, so its WebP is a PNG: the artifact's
`Content-Type` says what it is.

full_page.description:
False, the default: the visible viewport, which no page can
observe. True: the whole document, which fires `resize` in the page
on chromium; the result names that side effect.

ScreenshotStep.description: Take a screenshot at this point of the flow.

oneOf.description: How it is taken.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

ScrollEndField.description: Why the scrolling of a page ended.

depth.description: How far down to end, as a share of the document's height.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

ScrollView.description: How the scrolling of a page ended (spec §10.4).

ended_by.description:
`depth` (as far as it meant to go), `patience` (its patience ended
first) or `page` (the page does not go further).

patience_ms.description:
The patience the persona had with this page, in milliseconds: how
long it would have gone on scrolling at most.

reached.description: How far down the document it came, from 0 to 1.

SelectStep.description: Choose an option of a select element.

selector.description: The CSS selector of the select element.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

findings.description:
What was found: the echo's comparison on the http path, the
sidecar's findings per page on the browser path. Null for a path
that was skipped.

score.description: The score of a browser self-test, from 0 to 100.

skipped.description: Why the path was not tested, when it was skipped.

verdict.description:
`passed`, `failed`, `inconclusive` (the test site could not be
read), or `skipped`.

SelftestRequest.description: What a self-test is to cover.

third_party.description:
Also use the echo and load the detection pages that others run
(`selftest.http.third_party_url`,
`selftest.browser.third_party_pages`). They see the address of the
persona's proxy. Never done on a timer, only when asked for here.

SelftestView.description: What a self-test of a persona found.

passed.description: Whether every path that was tested passed, and at least one was.

persona.description:
The persona after the test: a failure cools it, a pass ends a
cooling that waited for one.

SessionRequest.description: What a new session is to be.

domain.description: A host the session is for: the persona is one its policy allows.

id.description:
The id: 1 to 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, unique for this
key. Left out: the server makes one.

oneOf.description:
Which personas the session may be pinned to. Here both lists are
conditions: the persona is in one of the countries and on one of
the engines.

expires_at.description:
When it ends unless it is used before: ten idle minutes, and six
hours after it was opened at the latest (`sessions.idle_ttl`,
`sessions.max_lifetime`).

last_used_at.description: When it last served a request.

persona.description: The persona every request of the session is made by.

SitemapView.description: How reading one sitemap file went.

state.description:
`waiting`, `read` (a list of pages), `index` (a list of sitemaps),
`missing` (the site has none there), `sitemap_unreadable` (the
scout's browser cannot show what it is: a gzipped file in Chrome,
or no sitemap at all), `failed` (the request did not get through),
`no_scout` (no persona but the site's reader could have asked: it
was not asked for), or `not_read` (the crawl ended first, or the
site has more files than `crawl.max_sitemaps`).

urls.description: The addresses it named that the crawl took in.

StepView.description: What a step of a flow reports.

action.description: The step's action; `final` for the page the flow ended on.

duration_ms.description:
How long it took, in milliseconds, the persona's own time on the
page included.

ok.description: Whether the step succeeded; null while it has not run.

paced_ms.description: How much of that was the persona's dwell and thinking time.

TargetStep.description: A step that acts on one element: `click` or `hover`.

human.description:
False: done by the browser's driver instead of the persona's mouse
and keyboard, which a page can tell apart. Refused
(`driver_input_denied`) unless the policy of the flow's site has
`driver_input: true`.

selector.description: The CSS selector of the element.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

TimingView.description:
Time per phase of the last attempt, in milliseconds; null for a phase
that did not happen on the path taken.

connect_ms.description: TCP to the proxy and the tunnel (http path).

total_ms.description:
The whole attempt: on a browser render this includes the time the
persona spent on the page.

ttfb_ms.description: To the first byte of the response.

selector.description: The CSS selector of the input.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

WaitField.description: What a browser waits for before the page is captured.

extra_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait after everything else.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match an element afterwards.

WaitForStep.description: Wait for one condition: exactly one of the four is given.

network_idle.description: Until no request ran for half a second.

timeout_ms.description: The step's own budget in milliseconds; 30000 unless said.

url.description:
Until the page's address matches this pattern: `**` is anything,
`*` anything but a `/`, everything else is itself.

WaitUntilField.description: The lifecycle point a browser waits for.

WebhookField.description: Where a job's events are posted (spec §16.6).

progress_every.description:
Post `job.progress` whenever this many more items are over. Left
out: only the end of the job is reported.

secret.description:
The secret every delivery is signed with: 16 to 256 bytes. Kept
encrypted and never returned. `X-Kage-Signature` is `sha256=` and
the hexadecimal HMAC-SHA-256 of `<X-Kage-Timestamp>.<body>` under
it.

url.description:
The receiver: an `http` or `https` URL whose origin the operator
listed in `webhooks.allowed_origins`
(`webhook_origin_not_allowed` otherwise). Kage posts from its own
address, follows no redirect, and shows of this URL only the host
afterwards.

WebhookView.description: A job's webhook, as far as it is shown.

deliveries.description:
The newest events and how their delivery stands; empty in a
webhook's own body.

host.description:
The receiver's host. The rest of its URL is not shown again: a
path or a query often is a token.

progress_every.description: `job.progress` every so many items; null for none.

XhrField.description: Which responses of the page's scripts are kept.

content_types.description: Media types to keep, for example `application/json`.

max_bytes.description: The largest body kept per response, in bytes; a longer one is cut.

max_responses.description: The most responses kept per page.

XhrView.description: One response a script of the page fetched.

dropped.description:
Matching responses that were not kept because the page had more
than `xhr.max_responses`.

responses.description:
The responses that matched the request's filter: each with `url`,
`method`, `kind` (`xhr` or `fetch`), `status`, `content_type`,
`bytes`, `truncated`, and its body as `body` (text, when it is at
most 256 kB) or as `body_artifact` (an artifact's id).

api_key.description: An API key, made with `kage key create` or `POST /v1/admin/keys` and shown once. The scopes an operation lists are the ones the key needs; scopes are independent, `admin` implies no other.
